newsitem.title: USA: Oil futures lower in ACCESS as Iraqi crisis eases.
newsitem.headline: Oil futures lower in ACCESS as Iraqi crisis eases.

text.p: Oil futures were heading lower late Sunday after a weekend in which the Iraqi crisis showed signs of easing.

NYMEX October crude oil futures traded between $24.20 and $24.30 a barrel in the first hour of business on the off-exchange ACCESS system, down from Friday's settlement of $24.51. ACCESS trading began at 1900 EDT/2300 GMT.
"The situation appears to be easing but keep your eyes and ears peeled," said an oil futures trader at Merrill Lynch & Co. in New York.

After Friday's stand-down by Baghdad when it said it would not fire at U.S. planes patrolling the no-fly zones in Iraq, U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry said on Sunday that he did not expect Baghdad would do anything provocative for now.
Nevertheless, the situation remained tense and 5,000 U.S. troops were still headed to the Gulf, as was the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise.
"The situation is defusing and impact on the price of oil is not as fearful," said Gerry Samuels at ARB Oil in Los Angeles.
However, "it is factored into the market that Iraqi barrels are out for now and if there is a big sell-off tomorrow there is good support all the way down $23," Samuels added.
He noted that the bull market in oil over the past four or five months had been driven by strong demand in the U.S. and elsewhere and dwindling stocks, particularly of heating oil.

October heating oil futures were down 59 points at 67.94 cents a gallon in early ACCESS trading. October gasoline futures had not traded but were quoted at 63.80 bid, 64.30 offered, compared with Friday's settlement of 64.60 cents a gallon.
-- Tony McAuley New York Energy Desk 1-212-859-1620
